findings.claim: The recorded full-suite run no longer describes the merged head. test-results.md records run full-suite as commit=5a03978 'working tree with the wave-8 SRS evidence rows', tests=1534; the API 21 check lines of release-notes.md cite the same commit. The head 3806d59 runs 1561 tests (27 more, added by the terminal-review fix commits) and a 'working tree' reference cannot be reproduced. ReleaseResultsDocsTest.ops_REL_003_AC4 only asserts tests > 0 and exit=0, so it cannot detect that the record has gone stale.
findings.evidence: docs/release/test-results.md:98; docs/release/release-notes.md (API 21 checks); src/test/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/docs/ReleaseResultsDocsTest.java:185-190. Regression at 3806d59: 1561 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run ./gradlew build --rerun-tasks on the final committed head and rewrite the full-suite line and the three API 21 check lines with that commit hash and tests=1561 (no 'working tree' wording). Optionally have the docs test compare the recorded commit with git rev-parse HEAD~N ancestry or drop the exact figure, so the record cannot silently drift.

findings.claim: Java null-literal trap of the overloaded attribute accessor is documented for req and ctx but not for the WebSocket session, and not in any Javadoc. WebSocketSession.attribute(String, Object) and attribute(String, Class<T>) are overloads; ws.attribute("user", null) in Java binds to the Class<T> read overload, whose implementation dereferences the null type and throws NullPointerException instead of removing the key. websocket.md states 'attribute(key, value): null is cleared' with no caveat, while request.md and lifecycle.md carry the warning. The Javadoc of the three interfaces says 'a null value removes the key' with no caveat either.
findings.evidence: docs/api/websocket.md:130-131; NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/WebSocketSession.java:43-47; NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/DefaultWebSocketSession.java:516-518 (DefaultRequest.wrapper(type) -> type.isPrimitive() NPE); docs/api/request.md:181 and docs/api/lifecycle.md (attribute section) for the documented counterpart.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same sentence as request.md to the websocket.md attribute table (and to the Javadoc of the three attribute(key, Object) declarations): pass a typed null variable or (Object) null. A Java user hits this at runtime only; no compile-time signal exists.

findings.claim: Failure atomicity of the configurer methods is inconsistent. multipart, webSocket and sse run the configurer on a copy and keep it only when it returns (their Javadoc says so), but server(...) and accessLog(...) run the configurer on the live options object. A configurer that throws part-way (for example app.server(o -> o.maxWorkers(10).maxSseStreams(0)) which throws IllegalArgumentException from the second call) leaves maxWorkers already changed, so a caller that catches the IllegalArgumentException and continues starts the app with a half-applied server configuration.
findings.evidence: NaruServe-api/src/main/java/com/snoworca/naruserve/internal/DefaultRestApp.java:229-258 (reconfigure on a copy) versus :367-383 (accessLog and server mutate accessLogOptions / serverOptions in place); RestApp.java Javadoc of multipart/webSocket/sse ('keeps the copy only when it returns') versus server/accessLog ('Runs configurer at once ... calls apply in order').
findings.suggested_fix: Either give DefaultServerOptions and DefaultAccessLogOptions a copy() and reuse reconfigure(...), or state in the server/accessLog Javadoc and docs/api/app.md that a throwing configurer leaves the options partly applied. The first is small: both classes are plain field holders.
